significance: A Shaiva temple at Mhaswad in Satara district, about 56 km from Pandharpur, attributed to the Badami Chalukyas and completed on its second side in 1738 by their descendant Dubal of Karad. Its Mhaswad Yatra, with a chariot of Siddhanath and crowds smeared in pink gulal, draws devotees from across India.
